$description: The checkable rules, as data. Every condition in contract.md has exactly one machine-readable entry here and is evaluated in exactly one place (check.mjs). Reasoning for any of these lives in decisions.md; measured results live in outcomes.md. Nothing here restates a value that a token file already holds.

type_bounds.$description: F3. Bounds the DTOS 2025.10 value schemas impose, held here rather than as literals in check.mjs, so the checker states no number of its own. Source: schemas/src/2025.10/format/values/*.json.

manifest.$description: B4, B5. One emitted CSS home now (the package the portfolio and Metis bind); no second copy to drift from. It stamps the manifest version on its first line (B5, extracted with the pattern below), and B4 rebuilds the CSS from source in memory and byte-compares the committed file to it, so a source edit that was never rebuilt cannot pass. The version's single home is packages/ame-tokens/ame.json.

naming.$description: N1. Every path segment. Lowercase, digits, single hyphen or underscore as separator. DTOS additionally forbids '.', '{', '}' and a leading '$' in any name; F5 checks those.

synonyms.$description: N2. One word per concept, across token paths and the repo's own exported symbols (Deissenboeck & Pizka's name-to-concept bijection; STANDARD.md N3). Each pair names the canonical word for a concept and the deprecated synonym that must not enter a new identifier. An identifier is tokenized on '-', '_', '.', '/' and camelCase boundaries; a deprecated word appearing as one of those tokens fails N2 unless the whole identifier is listed in `waived`. Vendored code (components/ui) is out of scope: its names are the upstream's call, not this repo's, the same exemption R-8 gives vendored files. Scope note: this reads identifiers, not Tailwind class strings or CSS custom-property call sites, so a `bg-*` utility class is untouched.
synonyms.waived_because: Each waived name is a bound token deliverable: a rename is a consumer migration, global-or-nothing (DECISIONS R-1's boundary on CSS custom-property renames), so the abbreviation stays until a dedicated migration order. The two concepts already carry both spellings in the tree, background/bg and button/btn, and the canonical is the fuller word the semantic role home and the component symbols already use. N2 blocks a third occurrence from landing, which is what the ratchet is for.

layering.$description: L1 to L3. A layer may reference only the layers listed. literalTypes lists the $types a layer may state outright rather than reference.

contrast.$description: C1 to C10, foreground over background, WCAG 2.2 relative-luminance ratio computed from the resolved token values. A translucent foreground is composited over its background before measuring. min 4.5 is AA for normal text; 7 is AAA. Each theme-following reading pair (a foreground with an -on-dark counterpart, over a ground listed in darkGround) is evaluated a second time as it resolves under [data-theme=dark], and checked against the same min (reported Cn-dark). The dark twin is derived from the -on-dark suffix and darkGround, so a new reading pair is covered in both themes without a second row. This closes the gap where C1's 7:1 held only the light half. Every pair declares a role (reading, fixed, chrome, or backdrop); a pair with no role fails, so a new row cannot default to unclassified and skip the cross silently. A role:reading pair must produce a twin; a missing or misspelled -on-dark sibling fails the check rather than passing quietly.

parity.$description: P1 to P3. A value with a second home in hand-written source. The token is the home; the literal must equal it. Each entry names the file, the pattern that finds the literal, and the token it must match.

duplication.$description: D1. A generated custom property re-declared in hand-written CSS is a second home for one value. Exceptions are values the token layer cannot hold: a runtime-switched assignment, or an asset.

allowed_because.--port-glass-fg: Runtime-switched between two tokens by [data-backdrop]. The values are tokens; only the assignment is CSS.
allowed_because.--port-glass-halo: A text-shadow the design sets to none on every surface. No second value exists to hold.
allowed_because.--port-panel-w: The base width is component.accessibility.width; the >=768px override is a calc() over the grid, which has no token form.
allowed_because.--ask-w: A local alias inside the anchor's centring math. Reads --port-panel-w; holds nothing.

restated.$description: D2. D1 catches a re-declared custom property. It cannot see a hand-written literal that happens to equal a token's resolved value, which is the same second home wearing different syntax: the nav pill and the work card each restated a shadow recipe the token layer already held, and the gate passed. Compared by numeric signature (the ordered numbers in the value) so rgba(16,19,25, 0.04) and rgb(16 19 25 / 0.04) are recognised as one value. min_numbers keeps single scalars from matching everything.

shipped.$description: G1. A placeholder that survives into emitted HTML says on its face that the page is unfinished, so it must never reach a deployed route. Evaluated only in --shipped mode, after next build, against the emitted app tree. STANDARD.md C5 is the same condition at repo scope; this is its one evaluation site.
shipped.$pattern_note: A bare \[\[ also matches React Server Component payload nesting (`[[["",{"children"`), which every Next 16 route emits, so it flagged 40+ routes that hold no placeholder. The pattern requires a bracketed identifier, which is the shape the source placeholders actually use ([[META_DESCRIPTION]], [[year]]). STANDARD.md C5's own grep is the untightened form; this is its one evaluation site and the tightening is decision D-15.

scales.$description: S1 to S5. Every literal of a scaled kind found in portfolio source must be a member of that scale. Reported as drift with a baseline rather than as a hard failure: Tailwind arbitrary-value classes can introduce a literal without touching this directory, so the count is a measurement that must not grow, in the shape CLAUDE.md uses for duplication.

binding.$description: U1. The deliverable standard's allowed binding paths, as a tripwire. Surfaces bind semantic and component tokens; only tokens bind base tokens. A surface reading a base custom property resolves fine by name and violates the layering the deliverable list publishes, so the gate and the deliverable list agree by construction. The base-name set is derived from the token tree at check time, never restated here or in check.mjs. Aliases are not base names: an alias is a spelling the surface is meant to bind.

uses_graph.$description: U2 to U4. The Parnas acyclic, layered uses-graph, extended off the portfolio surface that U1 already guards. The base-name set is DERIVED from the token tree at check time (the base tier names itself), never a prefix list: base and semantic share first segments (--border, --font, --duration each appear in BOTH tiers), so a prefix would misclassify a semantic token as base. Vendored components/ui is out of scope (R-8), the portfolio surface is U1's, and the emitted token CSS is the supplier, not a consumer. Source: STANDARD.md M (Parnas 1972, the acyclic uses-graph); DECISIONS R-26.

base_read.$description: No file in the app/components tree reads a base-tier custom property. U1 is this rule on the portfolio surface; U2 is the same rule on the rest of the tree (the /system shell and the shared ame chrome). Base binds base; a surface binds semantic or component.
base_read.waived_because: components/ame/* are the shared chrome (AmeNav, AmeFooter; R-12), tone-portable across the portfolio and the metis-marketing sister ground. Repointing these five base reads onto semantic or component roles is a scoped change: each replacement must resolve on BOTH grounds, and the marketing site syncs the generated CSS, so the repoint is a consumer migration owed to a dedicated order, not this check-adding pass (CLAUDE.md 9, the honest deferral). U2 waives the five known reads by name and blocks a sixth from landing. Follow-up: a dedicated order repoints components/ame off base and removes these waivers.

lib_no_app.$description: No lib/ module imports from app/. lib sits below app in the layered uses-graph, so a lib->app edge would make the graph cyclic. Matches @/app, @/app/*, and relative ../app paths.

surface_no_system_tokens.$description: No portfolio surface imports a lib/*-tokens design-token module. The portfolio DTOS token system and the lib/*-tokens /system design system are two homes for 'design tokens', adjudicated as two concepts in DECISIONS R-25. A portfolio-surface import of a lib/*-tokens module would merge them into a hidden third binding; this keeps the two concepts two.

clients.$description: H1. A token nothing consumes is a clause with one signature. A client is: a var() in portfolio source, another token's reference, an alias, or a named invariant that reads the token. The count of clientless tokens is a measurement, recorded in outcomes.md, and must not grow.

invariant_clients.$description: Tokens whose client is an invariant rather than a call site. A closed scale is consumed whole by the check that admits nothing outside it.
invariant_clients.dither: derived:--port-dither-noise (build.mjs serializes frequency and octaves into the feTurbulence URI)

lint.$description: Code-quality thresholds for eslint.config.mjs (WO-6.1, decision R-23, superseding tokens/decisions.md D-12). This file is the one home for the numbers; eslint.config.mjs reads them with readFileSync so the config states no threshold of its own, the same relation deliverables.md sets for the gate. Evaluated by ESLint, not check.mjs. `complexity` is an ERROR set at the current measured cyclomatic maximum, so it is green now and only ever ratchets DOWN as deep functions are split. The three max_* entries are WARNING thresholds; their counts are baselined in tokens/lint-baseline.json under the same move-down-only rule as baseline.json (X1). max_params is 6, STANDARD.md M2's stated limit, so a seventh parameter warns.

structured_data.$description: STANDARD.md D5 (WO-7.4, decision R-30). The data for the JSON-LD entity-graph checks. Evaluated by tests/json-ld.test.tsx, not check.mjs, the same way `lint` is evaluated by ESLint: this file is the one home for the values, the checker reads them. The blacklist is superseded/replaced Schema.org properties that must never appear in an emitted node; every property maps to its live replacement, which the check names when it fails. proficiency_levels is the closed vocabulary a TechArticle's proficiencyLevel may draw from.

ame_taxonomy.$description: contract.md AM2 (DECISIONS R-55, R-57, R-65). The five docs tiers of the /ame brand design system (Foundations, Layouts, Components, Sections, Pages), disjoint from the /system taxonomy (`taxonomy` above). content/ame/meta.json is the one home for which page sits in which tier; this lists the tiers and, for a deliberately deferred tier, the recorded reason. AM2 in check.mjs (checkAmeTaxonomyRegistry) holds every declared tier non-empty (at least one page under its separator in meta.json) or carrying a deferred_because here, so a tier is never silently absent. A sub-group separator inside a tier (Lockups, Header, Footer) is a visual grouping in meta.json, not a declared tier; AM2 only requires the tiers listed here, so an extra separator is admitted and ignored (R-65 M5). tiers also supplies the valid-tier set AM1 checks a registry row's tier against. The developer-facing get-started (formerly the 'For developers' tier, R-65 M4) is now the /ame index page itself; the tier is retired and its binding steps live in the index.

ame_registry.$description: contract.md AM1, AM3 (DECISIONS R-57). The /ame brand registry as the single home the /ame docs and gate checks read, parallel to and disjoint from `registry` (the /system registry; no component in both, clause H). Rows live in content/ame/component-registry.json. AM1 (checkAmeTaxonomyRegistry): every .tsx file under scan_dirs, minus the excluded set, has exactly one registry row keyed by source, that row points at a real file, and its tier is one of ame_taxonomy.tiers; a row may also point at a file outside scan_dirs (the viewer under extra_note) as long as it resolves and carries a valid tier. AM3: every row with animated true AND status equal to playground_status ('documented') must name a `playground` field resolving to an existing file; this session every animated row is status 'deferred', so AM3 passes vacuously and binds in Phase 3. excluded is the exemption set: context providers and pure-logic sinks that are not documentable UI, named with the reason, the same shape as the vendored-ui exemption (registry's components/ui scope note).
ame_registry.extra_note: components/prototype-viewer/viewer.tsx carries a row too (the prototype viewer) though it sits outside scan_dirs; AM1 admits a row whose source resolves and whose tier is valid, so the viewer row passes without being part of the mandatory coverage scan.

excluded.components/portfolio/portfolio-theme.tsx: PortfolioThemeProvider / usePortfolioTheme — a React context provider and its hook, not a rendered UI component. It supplies theme state to the tree; there is no visual surface to document or give a playground.
excluded.components/portfolio/a11y-prefs.tsx: PortfolioA11yProvider / usePortfolioA11y and A11Y_DEFAULTS — a React context provider, its hook, and its default record. State plumbing, not a documentable surface (the visible accessibility UI is portfolio-accessibility.tsx, which carries its own row).
excluded.components/portfolio/session-activity.ts: PortfolioSessionActivity — a pure side-effect sink that returns null (a useEffect logging session activity). It renders nothing, so it is not a documentable UI component.

ame_registry.excluded_because: Three files under the scan dirs are not documentable brand components: two are context providers and one is a render-null side-effect sink. Documenting them would assert a UI surface where there is none, the inverse of the frontier-stub disclosure rule (CLAUDE.md 12). Each is named here with its reason, the same exemption pattern registry gives vendored components/ui. A fourth file added under the scan dirs that is a real component gets a row or fails AM1; adding a provider here is a deliberate, recorded act.

asset_budget.$description: contract.md K1 (WO-8.6, decision R-40). A per-class byte ceiling on everything under public/, so the 25 MB-SVG / 82 MB-GLB class of regression cannot land silently again. A file is classed by its extension; the classes and their byte ceilings are `budgets`. A file over its class ceiling is a K1 VIOLATION, not drift: it is a stated ceiling, not a count that may creep to a baseline. `waived` is the ratchet for assets that already exceed their ceiling and cannot be reduced in this check-adding pass; each names its current byte size and is owned by a reduction order (see waived_because). A waived file passes while it does not GROW past the recorded size, so the ratchet only ever moves down, the same rule X1 gives drift counts. Extensions outside every class (.html) are not assets this clause weighs. Sizes are on-disk bytes: an LFS pointer not materialised in a shallow checkout reads smaller than its ceiling and passes, which is correct because the check weighs what is present.
asset_budget.budgets_because: svg 500 KB matches WO-8.1's stated re-authoring target for the Kindle SVGs; the real vector SVGs in the tree top out at 59 KB (logo/lockup.svg). font 500 KB clears the two InterVariable variable woff2 files (~388 KB, legitimately larger for two axes) and the InterDisplay/NeueHaas cuts (~110 KB) while blocking a return of the ~900 KB TTF class. image 250 KB clears the endorsement thumbnails (152 KB) and avatars (~100 KB) and catches the one ~0.9 MB art cover. model 5 MB is the repo's V4 large-binary sensibility and a realistic DRACO-compressed GLB target, against the 82.7 MB uncompressed model.
asset_budget.waived_because: Four assets exceed their class ceiling today and are held at their current byte size by the ratchet until a dedicated reduction order shrinks them (CLAUDE.md 9, the honest deferral). kindle-mascot.svg (10.0 MB) and kindle-ux-collection.svg (15.0 MB) are almost certainly embedded raster in an SVG wrapper; re-authoring them to <=500 KB each is WO-8.1, and that outcome is what unblocks Agent 3 WO-3.2 (the V4 large-binary breach). iphone17-pro.glb (82.7 MB) waits on a DRACO/meshopt-compressed variant plus viewer lazy-load (WO-8.1, WO-8.5). frieren-manga.jpg (0.9 MB) waits on image optimization and the WO-8.7 display-size resize. Each waiver may not grow: a larger re-export fails K1, so the ratchet only ever moves down.

census.$description: contract.md section Z (WO-9.1, decision R-50). The contract->invariants->check bijection, made machine-enforced instead of discipline-enforced. checkCensus parses the clause IDs declared in tokens/contract.md (the bold **A1** / **C1-C10** markers, en-dash normalized) and asserts each one has a census record below; a record names the invariants.json key that holds the clause's data (`invariant`) and the function in check.mjs that evaluates it (`check`), or carries a `structural` waiver naming the build.mjs mechanism that enforces it instead of a check.mjs branch. A clause with no record, a record naming a missing invariants key, or a record naming a check function absent from check.mjs fails Z1. A census record for a clause the contract no longer declares also fails, so the map cannot rot. threshold_scan is Z2: a grep-class scan asserting no threshold literal is hardcoded in the checker (deliverables.md: the gate imports its thresholds, never restates them), with a small allowlist of legitimate constants. Data here, logic in check.mjs, clause in contract.md, one home each.

A1.structural: build.mjs throws on a token missing $value before any check runs (contract.md: violating A1 stops the build). Reaching check.mjs proves it.

A4.structural: build.mjs (resolveValue) throws on an unresolved reference or a reference cycle before any check runs (contract.md: violating A4 stops the build).

B1.structural: build.mjs postcondition: each token is emitted exactly once under .portfolio-root. build.mjs is the single writer; a token cannot be emitted twice from one enumeration.

B2.structural: build.mjs postcondition: toCss serializes every value to a CSS literal; resolveValue leaves no {reference} unresolved, or A4 would have thrown.

B3.structural: build.mjs postcondition: each ALIASES entry emits var(--token) and throws if the alias does not resolve to exactly one token.

X1.structural: the drift ratchet's data home is baseline.json and runs.log, not invariants.json; checkRecord evaluates a baseline against the last logged run, so X1 has a check but no invariants entry by design.

threshold_scan.$description: Z2. No threshold literal hardcoded in check.mjs. The scan strips comments, strings, and regex literals, then flags any decimal literal or any integer >= min_integer that is not allowlisted. A threshold a clause compares against (a contrast minimum, a byte ceiling) lives in invariants.json; the checker reads it, never restates it. allow names the legitimate non-threshold constants that remain in checker code, each with its reason.

allow.1000: seconds-to-milliseconds unit conversion in checkScales convert()
allow.120: display truncation length for a violation message (slice(0, 120))
